extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) handling restriction/election practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how an examiner should require restriction/election under 35 U.S.C. 121 and 37 CFR (including treatment of linking/generic claims, content of restriction letters, telephone practice, timing, replies, traverses, and rejoinder).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must explain why there would be a serious burden if restriction not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner must explain why there would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must show by appropriate explanation one of the enumerated grounds (separate classification, separate status in the art, different field of search) or otherwise explain why a serious burden would result. Conclude restriction requirements with one of the required form paragraphs (8.21.01–8.21.03) asserting the burden reason selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate classification thereof
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate classification shows each invention has attained recognition in the art as a separate subject for inventive effort and a separate field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents need not be cited to show separate classification. If inventions have different classes/subclasses that support separate examination, this supports restriction. Use form paragraph 8.21.01 when concluding restriction on this basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate status in the art when classifiable together
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though classified together, inventions may show separate status in the art by recognition of separate inventive effort by inventors; patents may be cited as evidence of separate status and separate field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite patents or other evidence showing recognition of separate inventive effort. Use form paragraph 8.21.02 when concluding restriction based on recognized divergent subject matter or separate status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different field of search
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it is necessary to search for one invention in a manner not likely to find art pertinent to the other invention(s) (e.g., searching different classes/subclasses, electronic resources, or different queries), a different field of search is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The indicated different field of search must be pertinent to the subject matter covered by the claims. Patents need not be cited to show different fields of search. Use form paragraph 8.21.03 when concluding restriction on this basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking claims prevent restriction if allowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims are claims which, if allowable, would require rejoinder of otherwise divisible inventions and thus prevent restriction between those inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common linking claims include genus claims linking species claims and subcombination claims linking plural combinations. If a linking claim is allowable, the restriction between linked inventions must be withdrawn; nonelected claims that depend from or require all limitations of an allowable linking claim must be rejoined and fully examined. If restriction is predicated upon nonallowability of linking claims, applicant may retain nonelected claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of linking claims (examination and rejoinder)
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims must be examined with and are considered part of the elected invention. When all claims directed to the elected invention are allowable, should any linking claim be allowable the restriction must be withdrawn and appropriate rejoinder conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon indication of allowability of linking claims, cancelations may be reinstated by amendment and will be examined in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104; amendments before final rejection or allowance are entered as a matter of right; later amendments governed by 37 CFR 1.116 and 1.312. Warning: claims in continuations/divisionals that are anticipated by or include all limitations of an allowable linking claim may be subject to provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections over the instant application's claims. When a restriction is withdrawn, 35 U.S.C. 121 provisions no longer apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species: identify generic claims and species; require election under 35 U.S.C.121
rubrics_metrics.description: Where restriction between species is appropriate, the examiner should identify generic claims (or state none present), clearly identify each disclosed species to which claims are to be restricted, and require applicant to elect a single disclosed species under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species are preferably identified by figures or examples; if absent, state mechanical means, particular material, or other distinguishing characteristic. If species cannot be conveniently identified, group claims by species. Provide reasons why the species are independent or distinct. Advise applicant of requisites of a complete reply and of rights under 37 CFR 1.141. A reply should include a proper election and listing of all claims readable thereon; arguments that a claim is allowable or that all claims are generic are non-responsive unless accompanied by an election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and completeness of restriction requirement letter (outline A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirement letters must provide a clear, detailed record demarcating restricted inventions and include specified sections (statement of requirement/statute, identification/grouping of claims, descriptions, classification, disposition of ungrouped claims, reasons for independence/distinctness, reasons for insisting on restriction, and summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline: (A) Statement of requirement and that it is under 35 U.S.C. 121; (1) identify groups; (2) list claims in each group; (3) short description of subject matter for each group and type (product/process/subcombination); (4) classify each group. (B) Account for claims not grouped (linking, other ungrouped claims, disposition). (C) Allegation of independence/distinctness with facts and demonstration (subcombination vs combination, process vs apparatus, etc.). (D) Provide reasons for insisting upon restriction (see separate items). (E) Summary statement covering independence/distinctness and reasons, advising as to reply required, and indicating effects of allowance/cancellation of linking/evidence/product claims. Use appropriate form paragraphs (8.14–8.20.02; 8.01/8.02 for species).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for insisting upon restriction (enumerated factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should provide reasons for insisting on restriction; acceptable reasons include: separate status in the art, different classification, same classification but recognition of divergent subject matter, divergent fields of search, or search required for one group not required for the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state which of these reasons apply and illustrate/demonstrate how they lead to a serious burden if restriction is not required. These reasons should be summarized in the conclusion form paragraph added to all restriction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of making restriction requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.142(a) indicates a restriction requirement 'will normally be made before any action upon the merits; however, it may be made at any time before final action.' Examiner should make a proper requirement as early as possible, preferably in the first action if need exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before making a restriction requirement after the first action on the merits, the examiner should consider whether there will be a serious burden if restriction is not required. A second/new requirement may be made later when it becomes proper even if applicant complied with a prior requirement. A previously withdrawn improper requirement may be repeated later if restriction becomes proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should make the restriction requirement; transfer if out-of-center
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement should be made by an examiner who would examine at least one of the inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner should not require restriction if none of the claimed inventions is classifiable in his/her Technology Center; such an application should be transferred to a Technology Center where at least one claimed invention would be examined. When inventions would be examined in different TCs, consult and obtain approval from all TCs involved before making the requirement; differences resolved by chain of command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone restriction practice procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner determines restriction should be made, formulate a draft indicating linking/generic claims, telephone the attorney/agent to request an oral election (with or without traverse) after they have time to consider, and arrange a follow-up call—generally within 3 working days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use telephone where requirement is complex, applicant is pro se, or election won't be made by phone. If attorney/agent objects to oral election or fails to respond, mail a restriction letter referencing the unsuccessful call. When an oral election is made, incorporate into Office action a formal restriction requirement including the election date, attorney/agent name, and a complete record of the telephone interview, followed by a complete action on the elected invention as claimed. Use form paragraphs 8.23/8.23.01 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action on the merits and reply periods for restriction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When only a nonfinal written restriction requirement is made, generally no action on the merits is given and a 1-month shortened statutory period (minimum 30 days) will be set for reply; this period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a). The Office action making the restriction requirement final ordinarily includes an action on the merits of the elected invention claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restriction/election is made via telephone and applicant makes oral election, the written record will be accompanied by a complete action on the merits of the elected claims. When preparing a final action where applicant traversed the restriction, see MPEP § 821.01. If elected invention claims are found allowable and no nonelected invention is eligible for rejoinder, include cancellation of nonelected claims and close prosecution (notify via PTOL-37 and Ex parte Quayle/PTOL-326 for formal matters). Before canceling nonelected claims, ensure no allowable linking/generic claims or rejoinder eligibility exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and reply requirements; traverses
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply must respond to each point raised by the examiner and may include a traverse or compliance. A traverse is a statement of reasons why applicant believes the restriction is in error and must be complete per 37 CFR 1.111(b). Applicant must make a provisional election even when traversing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the reply must be reduced to writing, distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors, and reply to every ground of objection/rejection. A mere broad allegation that the requirement is in error does not comply; failure to distinctly and specifically point out supposed errors results in the election being treated as an election without traverse. To preserve right of petition (37 CFR 1.144), the applicant must traverse; to reserve right to petition election must be made with traverse. Use form paragraph 8.22 in Office actions containing restriction requirements to inform applicant that reply must include (i) an election and (ii) identification of claims encompassing the elected invention. If traversing on patentable distinctness grounds, submit evidence or identify evidence on record showing obvious variants or clearly admit that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make restriction requirement complete and clearly demarcated
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide a clear and detailed record of the restriction requirement to permit determination whether claims in a continuing application are consonant with the restriction and subject to double patenting prohibitions; particular claim limitations and reasons supporting restriction should be mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read all claims to determine what they cover. Identify separate inventions by grouping claims with short descriptions of total extent of invention claimed in each group, specifying type or relationship (process, subcombination, product, etc.), and indicate classification or separate status (class/subclass). While every claim should be accounted for, omission or misgrouping will not affect a proper final requirement if correct disposition is otherwise clear. Generic/linking claims should not be associated with any one of the linked inventions since they are examined with the elected invention.
